name: Wine distillation at Salerno
summary: Treatises linked to Magister Salernus of the medical school of Salerno describe distilling wine into aqua ardens around 1100 to 1150, an early European record of spirits.
description: A scholarly article says that treatises of Magister Salernus, of around 1100 to 1150, describe distilling wine into aqua ardens, burning water, and that he was distilling alcohol by the first half of the twelfth century. The distillation was inefficient and the distillate was probably mostly water. The article is a secondary study of later alchemical recipes, so the manuscript basis of the Salernitan treatises is still to be checked.

impact.note: European spirits spread through Europe and its colonies, but other regions' spirits are not shown to descend from Salerno (reach 2, lowered from 3); a stronger form of an existing drink (depth 1); alcohol as solvent and medicine fed pharmacy and early chemistry (generativity 2, from general knowledge, not the cited article).

date.label: c. 1100 to 1150 CE
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: Treatises of Magister Salernus, dated around 1100 to 1150, describe distilling wine into aqua ardens; he is named for the medical school of Salerno.

evidence.supports: His treatises around 1100–1150 describe wine distillation (aqua ardens). The School of Salerno was an early institution

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: The Latin manuscript and edition of the Salernitan treatises describing aqua ardens, which this secondary article cites (through Rasmussen 2014 and Moran 2005) but does not reproduce.
Rival early evidence: Arabic accounts of distilling wine, Gandhara stills (c. 150 BCE to 150 CE) and Jin-period distilled liquor in China, none of them opened here.
Relationship of the Salerno method to Arabic alembics.
The article is in volume 39 (2025) of the journal but was published online in March 2026.

research.note: The source does not say where Salerno's distillers learned the method, and earlier claims for distilled alcohol in the Arabic world, Gandhara and China were not examined, so neither independence nor priority is settled.
